claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC alloy.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy contains no oxide dispersion.
The baseline alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
Introducing 0.5–1.0 vol% Y2O3 through high-energy ball milling and HIP can create a uniform nanoscale oxide dispersion in TiVNbTa.
The Y2O3 particles will remain stable in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix at elevated temperature.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles act as pinning sites for dislocations.
Dispersed Y2O3 particles pin grain boundaries and inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
The oxide dispersion impedes dislocation climb, recovery, and grain growth at elevated temperature.
Suppressing dislocation and grain-boundary-mediated deformation will reduce high-temperature softening and creep.
The Y2O3-modified alloy may retain a yield strength above approximately 500 MPa at 1273 K.
The Y2O3-modified alloy is expected to have greater compressive strength than the approximately 423 MPa baseline at 1273 K.
The strengthened alloy is expected to maintain significant plasticity while its high-temperature strength increases.
Operations around 1273 K and strains up to 30–40% represent applicable boundary conditions for a TiVNbTa intermediate layer between W and CuCrZr.
Non-uniform oxide dispersion or detrimental secondary-phase formation may reduce the intervention's effectiveness.
